title: Smart Energy Meter
tagline: Turns minute-level electricity readings into a bill forecast, anomaly alerts and concrete ways to save.
overview: A Streamlit app that takes a CSV of household power readings, works out monthly consumption and the bill under a configurable tariff, forecasts next month’s bill with linear regression, flags abnormal readings with Z-scores and attributes them to devices, and finds idle or overused appliances with an estimate of what that waste costs.
problem: An electricity bill tells you how much you spent, not why. Without device-level insight it is hard to know which appliance caused a spike, what next month will cost, or where power is being wasted while nobody is using it.
motivation: Smart meters produce exactly the data needed to answer those questions. The project explores how far a lightweight analytics pipeline can go with nothing more than a CSV of readings.
objectives: Estimate the monthly bill from raw readings with a configurable tariff and fixed charge
Forecast the next month’s consumption and bill
Detect abnormal consumption and identify which device caused it
Find idle or wasteful device usage and estimate potential savings
features: CSV upload with a minute-level timestamp, total active power and optional per-device columns (`*_w`)
Monthly energy and bill table: energy charge at ₹/kWh plus a fixed charge from sanctioned load
Next-month bill prediction with scikit-learn Linear Regression over monthly totals
Z-score anomaly detection (|z| > 2) with primary and top-3 contributing devices
Idle-waste detection: sustained low-power runs below a % of each device’s 99th-percentile peak, with wasted kWh and ₹ savings
Overuse and unusual-hours detection per device
Smart insights: peak hour, average daily use, highest-consuming device
All thresholds adjustable from the sidebar

decisions.title: Statistical baselines first
decisions.detail: Z-scores and linear regression are transparent, fast and easy to explain to a non-technical user — a sensible baseline before heavier models.

decisions.title: Peak-relative idle threshold
decisions.detail: Idle is defined relative to each device’s own 99th-percentile power, so a fridge and a TV are judged on their own scale.

decisions.title: Everything tunable
decisions.detail: Tariff, idle percentage and minimum idle duration are sidebar inputs, because the right values differ between households.

decisions.title: Streamlit for delivery
decisions.detail: Streamlit made it possible to ship an interactive, deployed analysis tool without building a separate front end.

challenges.challenge: Datasets with and without device columns
challenges.solution: Device-level features are enabled only when `*_w` columns are present; otherwise the app explains what it needs.

challenges.challenge: Separating real waste from normal standby
challenges.solution: An idle event must last a minimum number of consecutive minutes below the device-specific threshold.

challenges.challenge: Explaining an anomaly, not just flagging it
challenges.solution: Each flagged reading is attributed to the device contributing most at that minute, plus the top three.

testing: The repository ships a 10,000-row, minute-level sample dataset with six device columns for trying every feature.
Deployed on Streamlit Community Cloud for hands-on use.
No automated test suite yet, and the forecast has not been evaluated against held-out months.
limitations: Linear regression on monthly totals needs several months of data and cannot capture seasonality.
A fixed |z| > 2 rule assumes roughly normal readings and will over-flag in naturally spiky households.
Works on uploaded files rather than a live meter feed.
improvements: Seasonal forecasting (e.g. SARIMA or gradient-boosted models) with backtesting
Rolling or per-device anomaly baselines, or an Isolation Forest
Live ingestion from an IoT meter
Unit tests for billing and idle-detection logic
